be200799a3bcb1b8e94f4cf1d8bea50bbeea41e8.summary: Cofense Intelligence report, published 2018-06-28, on the Zeus Panda banking trojan, which it says targets Italian users. Infected browsers receive injected scripts when victims log into online bank accounts. The malware shows distraction screens, drains funds and hides the transactions. It also reaches accounts protected by two-factor authentication, including corporate accounts. The report says Zeus Panda rarely targets banks outside Italy.

be5f16a4a1558170bdd5877bfc221097ec6d1fe6.summary: SentinelOne analysis of RustBucket, a multi-stage macOS malware campaign. Earlier researchers attributed it with strong confidence to the BlueNoroff APT, which the report says is generally assumed to be a subsidiary of the DPRK group Lazarus. Stage 1 is an AppleScript dropper disguised as a PDF viewer. Stage 2 payloads, in Swift and Objective-C, fetch Stage 3. Stage 3 Rust binaries gather host information, add a LaunchAgent persistence mechanism and open a backdoor. The report stresses anti-analysis techniques and leaves some attribution and code-variation questions open.

bee575efddd40c5fb55d6d0a72fa4f6878c0c801.summary: BlackBerry Threat Intelligence describes LokiLocker, a limited-access ransomware-as-a-service family first seen in mid-August 2021, with about 30 affiliates. Samples are written in .NET, protected with NETGuard and KoiVM, and encrypt files with AES and RSA. Early samples were spread inside trojanized brute-checker tools. If the ransom is unpaid, the malware can wipe files and overwrite the Master Boot Record. The researchers say the possible Iranian origin may be a false flag. Most known victims are in Eastern Europe and Asia.
